docs.text: Welcome A privacy-preserving protocol to alert drivers about different events for a better driving experience, regardless of map platform. Why are We Creating this? When driving, alerts can be very usefull, whether they are used for more accurate journey time or avoiding congestion soon to occur due to an accident. When using other platforms, you location, speed, alert time and other metrics are sitting together, to be collected, used or in the worst case, stolen. We want to seperate an user from their location and alert. Also, by allowing any map provider to work with us, we create a better experience for everyone with more accurate alerts. High-level Structure flowchart TD subgraph map-provider[Map Provider] direction LR map-provider-server[Map Provider Auth Server] -->|optional| map-provider-db[Map Provider Database] end subgraph alert-server[Centralized Alert Server] direction LR alert-server-service[Post Endpoint] -->|stores alert information| alert-server-db[Database] alert-server-db --> |makes alerts avalible| alert-publish-server-db[Request / Publish Endpoint] end client[Client] -->|proxies through| map-provider map-provider -->|forwards stripped & authenticated request| alert-server Client When posting, the alert information (location, type) are encrypted to only be seen by centralized server. Requests are proxied through their map provider. Map Provider Service Mainly to provide authentication and rate-limiting features that protect the centralized alert server Verify users in whichever way the service wants, then if verified, the still encrypted alert information is forwarded to the alert server. Alert Server Only has to trust map providers. Publishes alerts in batches to further obsfuscate requests.
